mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every hard graph admits floor(S_m) owned unit carriers and one global remainder omega; the integer deficit is at most floor(S_m), while omega is discharged once by the strict extremal edge inequality.
would_close: outer-A gate R_A<=S_m with exact rounding
mechanisms.kill_test: Odd-n examples and two disjoint tight circuits: kill if omega is charged twice or no strict integer margin absorbs it.
mechanisms.status_evidence: Odd-n rounding kill does not refute a single globally owned remainder discharged by a strict integer margin; such a margin remains unproved.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The weighted carrier incidence matrix is totally unimodular on every hard maximum-witness graph, so every feasible S_m-mass fractional payment has an integral demand-covering vertex.
mechanisms.kill_test: Search the smallest odd cycle minor and three-demand/two-carrier fractional instance; any nonintegral vertex or unmatched integral demand kills universality.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: one demand split over two half-capacity carriers is fractionally feasible but has no integral carrier assignment.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: All integer Hall cuts have one common strict surplus exceeding the single global rounding error 1-{S_m}; hence floor(S_m) carriers suffice simultaneously.
would_close: rounded Hall cuts without local error accumulation
mechanisms.kill_test: Glue many locally tight cuts sharing global slack; kill if any cut has surplus zero or if strictness depends on the chosen circuit.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: exact Hall cuts can have zero surplus, so no common strict margin absorbs a positive rounding error.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The union of internal-low edges and mixed high anchors in one hard graph contains ceil(Phi(n,e)) edges of distinct colours with pairwise internally vertex-disjoint C7 completion certificates whenever R_A>S_m.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test common-bottleneck path complexes and the n=14 hard graph; reused completion vertices or edges kill the disjoint-certificate claim.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: compatible outputs may share one path bottleneck; disjoint completion certificates are not inherited.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The low-edge/high-anchor exchange graph has matching number at least ceil(Phi(n,e)) whenever R_A>S_m; matched outputs are distinct-colour pairwise-C7-compatible edges.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use an exchange graph with a common anchor bottleneck; kill if scalar R_A excess coexists with matching rank below ceil(Phi).
mechanisms.status_evidence: The scalar counterprofile is not graph-realizable; a matching theorem in the actual low-edge/high-anchor exchange graph remains unrefuted.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The anchor-conflict graph has maximum degree o(I_mix) in every hard branch, while I_mix plus the dense internal-low alternative forces an independent compatible family of size ceil(Phi).
mechanisms.kill_test: Clique-chain and shared-completion bottleneck models; a linear-size conflict clique kills the degree claim.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: no inherited hypothesis bounds the conflict graph degree; a common-bottleneck clique has linear degree.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every minimal Hall-deficient B circuit owns an A diagonal whose anticomplete rectangle forces one previously unused actual B-reserve pair adjacent to that circuit.
would_close: one-carrier creation for every minimal deficit
mechanisms.kill_test: Replay the graph-realizable three-colour/two-token circuit and enumerate licensed rectangle outputs; kill if all outputs are occupied or shared.
mechanisms.status_evidence: Inherited graph-realizable three-demand/two-token circuit has no new licensed one-step output; see round2 evidence and evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: From every unmatched demand, the typed alternating creation graph reaches a free actual carrier; alternating cycles admit an ownership-preserving uncrossing that strictly shortens the path.
mechanisms.kill_test: Crossing circuits and closed two-token alternating cycles; kill on a terminal strongly connected component with no free carrier.
mechanisms.status_evidence: One-step creation is killed, but no theorem or actual countermodel excludes a longer graph-derived alternating path ending at a free carrier.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The boundary missing-pair map from mixed anchors has fibre size one after quotienting identical A diagonals, and its image avoids the already occupied canonical B reserve.
mechanisms.kill_test: Rectangular blow-ups and shared-boundary anchors; two distinct owners mapping to one B pair or an occupied image kills the claim.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: rectangular blow-up data allow arbitrarily many owners to share one boundary pair absent a uniqueness hypothesis.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The typed circuit-overlap hypergraph can be uncrossed to a forest without changing any demand neighbourhood, carrier ownership, or use of the one global rounding cell; local creation then globalizes without reuse.
would_close: global nonreuse across all tight circuits
mechanisms.kill_test: Two crossing circuits sharing one A owner and one B carrier; kill if every forest replacement loses a legal arc or duplicates an atom.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/ROUND3_MECHANISM_FALSIFICATION.json: crossing circuits share an owner and carrier; lossless forest uncrossing has no exchange axiom.
